I am an old man with no book learning, but I know this land well. My beans plot is small, only 0.25 hectares, and it is intercropped with my other crops, so I do not need to buy chemical fertilizer because the beans will draw nitrogen from the air and the manure from my few animals is enough to feed the soil. I save my own seed every year because the improved seeds from the agro-dealers cost too much money, and I have learned that without spraying, the insects will eat the cowpea leaves and flowers before I can harvest, so I must buy some pesticide. We depend entirely on the rains here in the North West, and with my sons and grandchildren helping, we can manage the planting, weeding, and harvesting ourselves without hiring many workers.
